items.prompt: Wide shot at first light in the small beaten-earth courtyard of a poor Calcutta lane house, 1880s: on the left a closed weathered wooden door of the house with two worn stone steps; on the right exactly one woman holding a long straw broom low to the ground, paused mid-stroke, her body turned toward the closed door on the left, her face in three-quarter view looking at that door with a grave, sorrowful, unsmiling expression, lips pressed together. A tulsi plant on a clay pedestal and a brass water pot by the steps. The courtyard is enclosed by a low whitewashed mud-brick wall and a thatched lean-to roof, with only open pale dawn sky above the wall. She is Hemshashi's mother, a 40-year-old Bengali woman, careworn round face, red bindi, small gold earrings, an ivory-white cotton sari with a thin red border, its red-bordered end drawn up over her head and covering her hair down to the forehead, red blouse. Bengal, 1880s Calcutta. Palette pale gold, ivory, soft indigo; cool grey-blue dawn light turning gold at the wall top.
